name: Coercion Religious
overview: The Scriptures reveal instances where religious devotion was enforced through solemn covenants and severe consequences, as seen when Judah committed wholeheartedly to seek the LORD, with a decree that those who refused to seek Him should face death (2 Chronicles 15:12-13). This demonstrates a historical context of coercion in religious practice, underscored by public oaths and communal rejoicing upon faithful commitment (2 Chronicles 15:14-15). Similarly, King Nebuchadnezzar’s establishment of a golden image and his summoning of officials to its dedication (Daniel 3:1-2) highlights the imposition of idolatrous worship under royal authority, reflecting the tension between enforced religious conformity and true faithfulness to God.
